label: Google Sheets
agentGuide: Base path /v4; the id is the one in the spreadsheet's URL. Structure: GET /spreadsheets/<id>?fields=sheets.properties (titles, sizes). Read: GET /spreadsheets/<id>/values/Sheet1!A1:D50 (values[][] as strings; add ?valueRenderOption=UNFORMATTED_VALUE for numbers; ?majorDimension=COLUMNS). Write: PUT /spreadsheets/<id>/values/Sheet1!A1?valueInputOption=USER_ENTERED {"values": [["a", 1], ["b", 2]]} (USER_ENTERED parses numbers, dates and formulas as a user would); append rows: POST /spreadsheets/<id>/values/Sheet1!A1:append?valueInputOption=USER_ENTERED {"values": [[...]]}; clear: POST /spreadsheets/<id>/values/Sheet1!A2:Z:clear. Several ranges at once: GET /spreadsheets/<id>/values:batchGet?ranges=A1:B2&ranges=Sheet2!A1:C3. Create: POST /spreadsheets {"properties": {"title": "..."}}. Add a sheet, format, sort: POST /spreadsheets/<id>:batchUpdate {"requests": [{"addSheet": {"properties": {"title": "..."}}}]}. Quote sheet names with spaces: 'My sheet'!A1. Finding spreadsheets is Google Drive's job.
